text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The initiative underway now on the Cyprus issue is the most important one undertaken since 1974, says President Glafcos Clerides.
- Deputy Nicos Anastassiades is tipped to be the new chairman of (right-wing) Disy after the resignation of party chairman Yiannakis Matsis last week.
- Security takes centre stage in the proximity talks the United Nations started with the two sides last week.
- The intensive round of contacts underway to breach the impasse on Cyprus are still only exercises on paper, say diplomats.
- Ten-year-old boy who was initially diagnosed as having a stomach virus last week died on Saturday night after emergency surgery for a blocked colon.
- Iraqi oil is set to flow to Cyprus again.
- The west drags its feet over Albania. Germany and Britain veto the deployment of a multinational force to the country.
- Unemployment in the hotel sector was on the rise in 1996.
